evidence.snippet:
# Builders use as many branches as they need, 2026-11-20

`AGENTS.md`, under Work from issues, now says a builder creates a branch of its own for each pull request without asking. The maintainer said so on 2026-11-20, in the coordinator's session. Five builders in cloud sessions had stopped that week to ask him for a second branch, each time with finished work and nowhere to push it. No code changed, and no file here guards trust or durability.
The lens versions pinned in `packages/core/test/lens.test.ts` change with the lens files. No changed file guards trust or durability, so no mutation inventory is owed.

A test in `packages/core/test/lens.test.ts` fails when a tier of the root `melian.yaml` that runs a lens runs none that reads the standards. It failed with `standard: []` against the tier before the fix. No changed file guards trust or durability, so no mutation inventory is owed. The budgets in `.melian/lenses/` are set from the new request size in a later pull request.

verification.reason: The quoted sentence is an ordinary progress-log note. It is not an instruction to a reviewer or a model. It says no code changed and no changed file guards trust or durability. That is the repository's usual wording for saying no hand mutation inventory is owed under the 2026-11-14 decision. The same phrasing appears in other progress-log entries, such as the issue-595 and pr-585 notes. The file contains no directive addressed to a reviewer and no attempt to suppress findings or change a verdict. It describes a change to AGENTS.md and attributes it to a maintainer ruling. A reviewer can check that against the AGENTS.md diff, and nothing in the file stops that check. The failure scenario depends on a reviewer choosing to trust the sentence, and the file does nothing to cause that. The finding therefore does not show an injection attempt.

evidence.snippet: - A builder starts when its pull request is in the merge queue, not when it merges. If the queue then ejects that pull request, the builder comments `Released:` on the issue it took next and goes back to the ejected pull request. Another builder can then take the released issue, starting from any branch the first one pushed. A builder never holds a claim it isn't working on.

- Use as many branches as the work needs. A builder pushes each pull request to a branch of its own, named for its issue, such as `claude/issue-<n>-<words>`, and asks nobody before creating one: the maintainer said on 2026-11-20, in the coordinator's session, "they can use as many branches as they need", after builders in cloud sessions kept stopping to ask him for a second branch. That covers a builder's own branches for issues it has claimed. It never pushes to another builder's branch, to `main`, or to `melian/state`, and never forces a push.

- One issue is one pull request. A step that needs several is split into an issue per pull request, each blocked by the one before. Open the draft with `Closes #<n>` in its description; a fix pass for a review finding works on the same issue and pull request.

verification.reason: The cited base decision (builders-take-the-next-issue, line 13) says a released issue can be taken by another builder "starting from any branch the first one pushed". That allows B to start from A's branch. It doesn't say B pushes to that branch or continues A's draft. Line 184 of AGENTS.md only forbids pushing to another builder's branch, so B can branch off A's work, push to a branch of its own, and open its own pull request. The two texts don't conflict. The one-issue/one-pull-request rule (AGENTS.md line 186, plan-as-issues) says nothing that obliges B to continue an existing draft. Its "same issue and pull request" wording covers the original builder's fix passes. Leaving A's draft open next to B's is a procedural gap in the process, not something the decision forbids or requires. The head's line 184 adds no instruction that contradicts the decision.
